title: Von Neumann Architecture
welcome_lead: Inside the classic computer: CPU, memory and the stored-program idea.
meta_desc: IBDP CS adventure on von Neumann architecture, CPU components and buses.
final_note: Von Neumann: instructions and data share one memory!

concepts.def: Single memory for both data and instructions.
Directs operation of CPU and signals.
Fast storage location inside the CPU.

walkthroughs.body_html:
CPU contains ALU + CU + registers.

Memory holds program and data, connected via buses.

PC: next instruction. MAR: address. MDR: data buffer.

IR: current instruction. ACC: accumulator for ALU results.

Programs are loaded into the same memory as data.

This flexibility enables modifying programs at runtime.

numericals.q: How many registers explicitly named (PC, MAR, MDR, IR, ACC)?

free_texts.q: Architecture with shared memory for data and code?
